description: The Bangladesh Waste Database is a compilation of urban solid waste figures for Bangladesh produced by Waste Concern, a Bangladeshi organisation working on solid waste. Two editions are published, for 2014 and 2021. The 2021 edition, a 32-page report, gives waste generation by city type, waste composition, projections of urban population and waste, the land needed for landfills, greenhouse gas emissions from waste and faecal sludge generation, with maps and tables. Its coverage is national; the underlying database covers 340 municipalities. The two reports are free and available to download as PDF from the Waste Concern site; the underlying municipality-level database is only available on request, and no licence is stated. Caveats: figures are estimates built from per capita generation rates and surveys, not weighbridge records, and the latest edition dates from 2021. Simulation uses: sizing collection and landfill capacity for Bangladeshi cities, projecting waste growth under urbanisation scenarios and estimating methane from disposal sites. Related records: the global waste sector projections (data-global-waste-sector-1990-2050) put national figures in a wider frame, and the FAO food loss and waste database (data-fao-food-loss-and-waste-database) covers food waste specifically.
